claims.text: The city's December 2025 committee briefing says the program puts 100 AI-enabled cameras on sanitation brush trucks.
claims.quote: Implement 100 AI-enabled cameras on Sanitation brush trucks
claims.scope_note: City of Dallas Finance Committee deck, December 9th, 2025.

claims.text: The city says the cameras take photos as the truck drives at 25 to 35 miles per hour.
claims.quote: Take photos as it drives (25-35 MPH)
claims.scope_note: Stated in the city's deck. The film draws the truck as an illustration.

claims.text: The city says the software detects potential property issues from the images using computer vision and AI.
claims.quote: Automatically detect potential property issues from images using computer vision and AI
claims.scope_note: Describes the design in the city's deck, not a measured accuracy.

claims.text: The city's detection list includes bulk trash participation, tires, illegal dumping, graffiti, boarded windows and doors, and high grass.
claims.scope_note: The deck lists these conditions as what the software detects. The quoted excerpt is the first list item. The same slide lists tires, illegal dumping, graffiti, boarded windows and doors, and high grass.

claims.text: The city says the cameras blur faces and license plates.
claims.quote: Blurred faces and license plates for privacy.

claims.text: The city's briefing says the program is not automated ticketing and that a human is in the loop for all actions.
claims.scope_note: City deck slide on what the program is not. The same slide says there is a human in the loop for all actions.

claims.text: The city's briefing lists maximizing voluntary compliance through educational notices as a purpose of the program.
claims.quote: Maximize voluntary compliance rate through educational notices
claims.scope_note: Stated purpose in the city's deck.

claims.text: The city's contract cost is $852,000 per year for 100 cameras and the associated technology and service.
claims.quote: The contract cost is $852,000 per year, which includes 100 cameras and all associated technology, installation, data services, maintenance, warranty, and replacement support.

claims.text: Fox 4 reports that a September 8th city memo says the cameras scanned 10,000 properties and that 57 citations were handed out at 34 properties.
claims.quote: 57 citations have also been handed out at 34 properties from what the cameras have scanned.
claims.scope_note: Press report of the September 8th memo. The memo itself was not retrieved. Fox 4 and the Dallas Express report the same count and the Dallas Morning News reports 57 citations at 34 properties.

claims.text: Fox 4 reports that the memo states a code officer inspects the property in person and gives the owner notice before a citation is issued.
claims.quote: The memo also states citations are only issued after a code officer inspects the property in-person and provides notice to the owner.
claims.scope_note: Press report of the September 8th memo, not the memo.

claims.text: The Dallas Morning News, republished by GovTech, describes the city's process as an AI flag, then an analyst review, then a city decision, then an officer inspection in person, and says a citation may be issued only after an actual violation is confirmed.
claims.quote: A code compliance analyst reviews the observation,
claims.scope_note: Dallas Morning News reporting republished by GovTech. The same list continues with the city workers' choice of no action, a courtesy notice or a case, then an in person inspection by a code officer.

claims.text: The Dallas Express reports that the city manager's memo says 39 of the 57 citations were issued in City Council Districts 4, 8 and 7 in Southern Dallas.
claims.quote: According to the city manager's memo, 39 citations, or 68%, were issued in City Council Districts 4, 8 and 7 in Southern Dallas.
claims.scope_note: Press report of the memo. The Dallas Express attributes the districts' demographics to NBC 5 and the film does not state them.

claims.text: The Dallas Morning News, republished by GovTech, reports that Dallas has not completed a comprehensive evaluation or return-on-investment analysis of the program.
claims.quote: Dallas has not completed a comprehensive evaluation or return-on-investment analysis.
claims.scope_note: Reported by the Dallas Morning News as of its September 17th article.

claims.text: Fox 4 reports that a briefing on the cameras from the city manager will take place on October 19th.
claims.quote: A briefing on the cameras from Dallas City Manager Kim Tolbert will take place on October 19.
claims.scope_note: Scheduled briefing. No agenda or outcome was retrieved and the film states neither.

claims.text: The Dallas Morning News, republished by GovTech, says a courtesy notice is not a citation or fine and gives the owner the chance to fix the problem before the city takes enforcement action.
claims.quote: A courtesy notice is not a citation or fine. It gives a property owner the opportunity to fix the problem before the city takes enforcement action.
claims.scope_note: Reported description of the notice. Press accounts conflict on the notice count and the film states none.
